correctness.rationale: In [1], Eq. (B16) gives the adopted deterministic weak-selection pair-approximation gradient and (B18) its stability test. Direct differentiation yields F_H(C); its derivative (H^2-2-HC)/(H+C)^3 has exactly the critical shape claimed, giving a necessary and sufficient strict four-interior-root criterion and radical formulas. The alternating flow signs and positive B-second-derivative multiplier classify the roots. The example has theta=17/64, H=3, C=(45±16sqrt(2))/17 and exactly two attractors. Independently evaluated benefit derivatives and bracketing reproduced four roots and signs in 141 cases; no finite test is used to certify all parameters.

originality.rationale: The precise four-root classification and cost/separation phase diagram for two increasing logistic stages is not reported in inspected [1] (single sigmoid) or [2] (well-mixed binary action and a different, increase-then-decrease double inverse sigmoid). Relevant mathematical records and earlier reported claims were compared by implication; no matching theorem located. General two-logistic mixture density theory may already subsume the analytic bimodality lemma; that ingredient is not independently claimed. Novelty is assessed with residual unindexed-literature risk.
residual_risks: An older equal-weight logistic mixture distribution theorem may give the same bimodality threshold, though the present claim also establishes the graph-game cost and investment regime.
Unindexed or inaccessible exact two-stage public-goods equilibrium analysis may exist.
The stability interpretation inherits pair approximation/weak selection from the motivating paper; it is not a finite-population stochastic theorem.

value.rationale: The exact sharp region for four distinct singular investments distinguishes two beneficial project stages from the one-sigmoid case: there are two attracting, locally evolutionarily stable cooperative-investment levels with an explicit basin boundary. Knowing the threshold separation and cost window identifies when multistable contributions are mathematically possible in the motivating evolutionary model, without a parameter-grid guess. This is a structural all-parameter classification rather than a routine small numerical example.
